common_name: Purple Magic Crape Myrtle (Color-Changing Purple Dwarf Crape Myrtle)

planting.note: Plant container plants in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Purple Magic is a compact, shrub-form crape myrtle in the same color-changing Magic series as Coral Magic, with flowers that deepen in tone as they age.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Purple Magic bears clusters of rich purple flowers that intensify in shade as the blooms age, part of a compact, shrub-sized crape myrtle series bred for smaller landscapes, foundation plantings, and large containers where full-size crape myrtles would quickly overwhelm the space. Its naturally rounded, dense habit needs little to no corrective pruning, unlike full-size types that are often disfigured by improper topping, and it shares the improved powdery mildew resistance of modern crape myrtle breeding. Water regularly through the first season to establish a deep root system; once established it is drought-tolerant and needs only occasional deep watering through the heat of summer.

common_name: Delta Jazz Crape Myrtle (Dark Purple Foliage Pink-Flowered Crape Myrtle)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Delta Jazz is part of the Delta series bred for dark, near-black foliage that holds color through summer heat.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Delta Jazz produces bright pink flower clusters that stand out sharply against deep chocolate-purple foliage, one of the darkest leaf colors available in the genus, giving the plant strong visual interest even before it flowers. Like other Delta series crape myrtles it holds its dark foliage color through the growing season rather than fading to green, and it reblooms over several weeks if spent flower clusters are removed. Its moderate size fits a smaller landscape tree role, and the naturally attractive vase-shaped form and exfoliating bark provide winter interest after leaf drop. Avoid severe annual topping ('crape murder'), which sacrifices the natural form; instead remove only dead, crossing, or downward-growing branches in late winter.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension — Crape Myrtle Cultivar Selection
North Carolina State Extension — Crape Myrtle Culture

common_name: Delta Flame Crape Myrtle (Dark Purple Foliage Red-Orange-Flowered Crape Myrtle)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Delta Flame shares the dark, near-black foliage of the Delta series with hot red-orange flowers for especially high contrast.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Delta Flame bears vivid red-orange flower clusters against dark, near-black purple foliage, one of the hottest color combinations in the Delta crape myrtle series, and holds its dark leaf color through summer heat rather than fading toward green. It reblooms over several weeks if spent flower clusters are deadheaded, and its moderate size and naturally attractive, multi-trunked vase shape with exfoliating bark suit it to use as a small specimen tree as well as a large shrub. Water regularly the first season to establish roots; established plants are drought-tolerant. Avoid severe annual topping, which sacrifices the plant's natural form and delays bloom — remove only dead, crossing, or downward-growing branches in late winter.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension — Crape Myrtle Cultivar Selection
North Carolina State Extension — Crape Myrtle Culture

common_name: Berry Dazzle Crape Myrtle (Dwarf Reblooming Magenta-Purple Crape Myrtle)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Berry Dazzle is part of the dwarf, reblooming Dazzle series bred for small-space landscapes and containers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Berry Dazzle bears clusters of rich magenta-purple flowers on a true dwarf crape myrtle that stays under 3 feet tall, part of the Dazzle series bred specifically for small foundation beds, low borders, and containers where full-size crape myrtles would be far too large. It flowers repeatedly from summer through fall, especially if spent blooms are removed, and holds a naturally tidy, mounded shape without the pruning most crape myrtles need to control size. Water regularly through the first season to establish a deep root system; established plants tolerate heat and drought well and rarely need more than occasional deep watering.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension — Crape Myrtle Cultivar Selection
